column2: The tribunes of the Communard Cities have gathered in Magritta, and for once they agree on something. Our cities have traded on the southern seas for longer than anyone remembers, yet every year newer merchants crowd into our waters: Tilean upstarts, Arabyan corsairs and the guildsmen of the north. They want to know what the High Tribune means to do about it.
Buy up the trading posts along the southern coasts.
Trade can wait. Arm the cities.
The Marienburg League is the real rival. Take them on.
Each Communard house with the coin to spare buys a trading post on the coasts of Estalia, Tilea, Araby or the Badlands, paying its old owner.
The Communards seize one of the Marienburg League's trading posts, and the two merchant powers become bitter rivals.
The Communard Concord

The Communard Cities of Estalia have bound themselves in a new Concord. Their houses are buying trading posts all along the southern coasts, and they pay in good silver, which makes them hard to refuse. The old masters of the southern seas mean to stay its masters.
The Communard Cities of Estalia have bound themselves in a new Concord, and its first act was to arm every guild and street. Whoever means to take the old free cities will find them ready.

The Communard Cities of Estalia have bound themselves in a new Concord and declared the Marienburg League their rival. Communard ships have already taken one of the League's trading posts. The two greatest merchant powers of the Old World are at each other's throats.
Interesting.
The Concord stands.
An agent of one of the Communard houses has bought our trading post. Their offer was too generous to refuse, and they made it clear that the next one would not be.
At least we were paid.
Communard ships have sailed into one of our trading posts, run up their colours and told our factors to leave. The Concord means to break the Marienburg League's hold on the seas.
They will regret this.

Five houses from five corners of the world hold Pigbarter: an Arabyan house from Copher, a Westerlander one from Marienburg, a Cathayan one, a Reman one and a Strigany one. Their town sits on the edge of the Black Gulf with greenskins, ogres and the Chaos dwarfs of the Dark Lands all around it. The houses have sworn a compact: they will pay for walls and a standing guard together, and they look to you to decide how to keep their neighbours at bay.
Pay the ogre tribes to keep the peace.
Raise a stockade and arm the houses.

Envoys of [pigbarter_neighbour.GetTitledName] stand at the gates of Pigbarter. Their master has noticed how rich the town has grown, and wants a share of it. They ask for fifty pieces of gold, which is not much as these things go. Refusing may make an enemy of them.
Pay them and pray they stay bought.
Pigbarter pays no one!
The Fall of Pigbarter

Pigbarter has fallen. The strange little trading town on the edge of the Black Gulf could not hold out against its neighbours forever, and its merchant houses have gone home: the Arabyans to Copher, the Westerlanders to Marienburg, the Remans to Remas, the Strigany to Sylvania, and the Cathayans back along the eastern roads to Cathay. Whatever its new masters build there, it will not be the same.
A pity. It was good for trade.
Communard Free Ports
The Communard houses are buying trading posts all along the southern coasts.
Communard City Militias
Every guild and street of the Communard Cities has been armed.
Rival of the Marienburg League
The Communard Concord is fighting the Marienburg League for the trade of the seas.
Ogre Peace
The nearby ogre tribes have been paid to leave Pigbarter alone, and some of them guard its roads.
Pigbarter Stockade
The merchant houses of Pigbarter have raised a stockade and armed their servants.

Pigbarter is under attack, and word has gone out along the trade roads. The houses' kin in Copher, Marienburg, Remas, Sylvania and far Cathay have answered: a ship has come in with gold and a company of sellswords, paid for until the fighting ends.
Blood is thicker than trade. Mostly.
The ogre tribes won't demand tribute from Pigbarter while the ogre peace holds.
They may lay claim to Pigbarter (less likely behind a stockade).
Pigbarter Compact
The five merchant houses of Pigbarter pay together for its walls and its guard.
Tribute Recently Demanded
A neighbour has demanded tribute from Pigbarter not long ago.
Kin Recently Sent Aid
The houses' kin abroad sent help to Pigbarter not long ago.
